description: The archetypal toadstool — a scarlet, white-warted cap that is as culturally iconic as it is chemically active. Ectomycorrhizal with birch and conifers across the Northern Hemisphere.
edibilityNotes: Contains the neurotoxins ibotenic acid and muscimol; ingestion causes a dose-variable delirient/sedative syndrome plus GI upset, not classical hallucinogenesis. Rarely fatal in healthy adults but genuinely dangerous. Traditional parboiling-and-discarding detoxification is practiced in some cultures but is not reliable or recommended.
habitat: Birch and conifer forests, often on poor/sandy soils
distribution: Native and widespread across the boreal and temperate Northern Hemisphere; introduced to the Southern Hemisphere (Australia, New Zealand, South America, southern Africa) with planted birch and conifers.
capColor: fading to orange or yellow with age or rain
speckled with white to pale-yellow warts

dangerousLookalikes.name: Amanita caesarea
dangerousLookalikes.note: Caesar's mushroom — a prized edible with a similar red-orange cap, but lacks white warts and has yellow (not white) gills/stem. Rain can wash the warts off A. muscaria, collapsing the distinction.
